question: In Tahngka Paintings, pictures of God _______ are drawn on clothes made of cotton or silk.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Buddha**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Buddha** is the correct answer for the deity depicted in Thangka paintings.
 
• Thangka paintings are a Tibetan Buddhist art form that often features images of the Buddha, bodhisattvas, and other deities.
 
• These paintings are typically created on cotton or silk fabric and are used for religious purposes, meditation, and to convey Buddhist teachings.
 
• Thangka paintings are known for their intricate detail and vibrant colors, and they play a significant role in Tibetan culture and spirituality.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Thangka paintings date back to the 7th century and are an important part of Tibetan Buddhist practice.
 
• They are often used as teaching tools, depicting the life of the Buddha, various influential lamas, and other deities and mandalas.
 
• Thangkas are typically kept unframed and rolled up when not on display, to protect them from damage.
 
• The creation of a Thangka is a meticulous process that requires a deep understanding of Buddhist iconography and symbolism.
 
• Thangka paintings are also a means of preserving and promoting Buddhist culture and heritage.
